tools.name: calculator_database_query
tools.short_description: Execute SELECT query against Calculator Pricing Database (read-only, safe)
tools.description: Execute SELECT queries against the Calculator Pricing Database (Supabase PostgreSQL with 8 tables, 690+ rows). Read-only operation - safe to use for data retrieval. BEFORE using this tool: Call calculator_database_get_schema_guide() to understand table structures, column names, JSONB field access patterns, and see 20+ example queries. This tool accepts raw SQL SELECT statements and returns results as list of dicts. Supports: Basic SELECT, JOINs, subqueries, CTEs (WITH), JSONB queries, aggregations. Includes: Safety validation (blocks non-SELECT queries), parameterized queries (prevents SQL injection), execution time tracking, automatic dataframe conversion. Common use cases: Get pricing parameters with variance analysis, retrieve calculator configurations, query product options with choices, find high-variance items, audit trail queries, cross-system analysis (pricing + options). Remember to: Cast JSONB fields to types (value_statistics->>'variance_pct')::numeric, check is_active=TRUE for current overrides, use array_agg() for one-to-many joins, include ORDER BY with LIMIT for consistent results.

sql.description: SQL SELECT query string (or WITH...SELECT for CTEs). Must start with SELECT or WITH. Can include: WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, LIMIT. JSONB access: Use ->> for text, ::numeric for numbers, @> for contains, jsonb_array_length() for array size. Table names: calculator_pricing_parameters, calculator_parameter_overrides, calculator_parameter_history, calculators_registry, product_options, product_option_choices, product_option_overrides, product_option_history. Always cast JSONB fields before sorting or numeric comparisons.

params.description: Optional tuple of parameter values for safe SQL parameterization. Use placeholders in sql string. Prevents SQL injection. Recommended for all queries with user input or variable values.

returns.description: Query result with success status, data array (list of row dicts), row_count, executed query string, and execution_time_ms. On error: success=False with error message and error_type

parameters.sql: SELECT parameter_name, base_value, (value_statistics->>'variance_pct')::numeric as variance FROM calculator_pricing_parameters WHERE (value_statistics->>'variance_pct')::numeric > 100 ORDER BY variance DESC LIMIT 5

examples.expected_result: Returns 5 parameters with highest price variance across calculators. Data includes parameter name, base value, and variance percentage.

examples.description: Get calculator's complete config with overrides

parameters.sql: SELECT c.calculator_name, c.parameters_used, array_agg(json_build_object('param', p.parameter_name, 'value', o.value)) as overrides FROM calculators_registry c LEFT JOIN calculator_parameter_overrides o ON c.calculator_name = o.calculator_name AND o.is_active = TRUE LEFT JOIN calculator_pricing_parameters p ON o.parameter_id = p.id WHERE c.calculator_name = %s GROUP BY c.id

examples.expected_result: Returns BollardSigns calculator with full parameter config and all active overrides

examples.description: Get product options with all choices for a calculator

parameters.sql: SELECT po.option_name, po.is_required, array_agg(json_build_object('title', poc.choice_title, 'price', poc.price, 'price_type', poc.price_type) ORDER BY poc.display_order) as choices FROM product_options po LEFT JOIN product_option_choices poc ON po.id = poc.option_id WHERE po.calculator_name = %s GROUP BY po.id ORDER BY po.display_order

examples.expected_result: Returns all product options for NotepadsA4 with nested choices array for each option

tools.name: calculator_database_modify
tools.short_description: Execute INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on Calculator Pricing Database (with safety checks)
tools.description: Execute INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE queries against the Calculator Pricing Database (Supabase PostgreSQL). Write operations with safety validations. BEFORE using: Call calculator_database_get_schema_guide() to understand table structures and constraints. ALWAYS include reason parameter for audit trail. Safety features: Blocks SELECT queries (use calculator_database_query instead), blocks dangerous operations (DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, DROP DATABASE), auto-commits changes, validates query types, tracks execution time. Common use cases: Update pricing parameter override values, insert new calculator parameter overrides, update product option choice prices, delete inactive overrides, bulk update pricing constants, modify calculator configurations. Automatic history logging: Changes to overrides and choices are automatically logged to history tables via database triggers. Remember to: Always include reason parameter for audit trail, use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection, check constraints before inserting (UNIQUE, FOREIGN KEY, CHECK), verify is_active flags for current values, test with SELECT first to preview changes.

sql.description: SQL INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE query string. Cannot be SELECT (use calculator_database_query for reads). Cannot include DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, or DROP DATABASE (blocked for safety). Can modify: calculator_parameter_overrides (update override values), product_option_choices (update prices), calculator_pricing_parameters (update base values), product_options (update option configs). Use WHERE clause carefully to target specific rows. Always use %s placeholders for variable values.

params.description: Optional tuple of parameter values for safe SQL parameterization. Use placeholders in sql string. REQUIRED for security - prevents SQL injection.

reason.description: REQUIRED: Explanation of why this modification is being made. Used for audit trail and compliance. Examples: 'Price increase due to supplier cost change', 'Correcting data entry error from Dec 15', 'Seasonal discount for holiday promotion', 'Updating to match current market rates'. Be specific and include context.

returns.description: Modification result with success status, rows_affected count, executed query string, execution_time_ms, committed flag, and reason. On error: success=False with error message and error_type

parameters.sql: UPDATE calculator_parameter_overrides SET value = %s, updated_at = NOW() WHERE calculator_name = %s AND parameter_id = (SELECT id FROM calculator_pricing_parameters WHERE parameter_name = %s) AND is_active = TRUE
parameters.reason: Price increase due to supplier cost change effective Dec 17 2025

examples.expected_result: Updates impos_setup value for BollardSigns calculator to $50.00, returns rows_affected=1

parameters.sql: UPDATE product_option_choices SET price = %s, updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = (SELECT poc.id FROM product_option_choices poc JOIN product_options po ON poc.option_id = po.id WHERE po.calculator_name = %s AND po.option_name = %s AND poc.choice_title = %s)
parameters.reason: Stock price increase from supplier effective Dec 17 2025

examples.expected_result: Updates Bond 80GSM stock price to $0.035 per sheet, database trigger automatically logs change to history

parameters.sql: INSERT INTO calculator_parameter_overrides (parameter_id, calculator_name, value, is_active, notes, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ((SELECT id FROM calculator_pricing_parameters WHERE parameter_name = %s), %s, %s, TRUE, %s, NOW(), NOW())
parameters.reason: Adding holiday season override for CustomVinylStickers extra arts fee

examples.expected_result: Inserts new override row, returns rows_affected=1, history automatically logged

workflow: Step 1: Call calculator_database_get_schema_guide() to understand table structures and constraints
Step 2: Use calculator_database_query() to SELECT current values first (preview)
Step 3: Write INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE query with correct table and column names
Step 4: Use %s placeholders for all variable values
Step 5: Prepare params array with values in correct order
Step 6: Write clear reason explaining why change is needed
Step 7: Execute with calculator_database_modify(sql, params, reason)
Step 8: Check success status and rows_affected count
Step 9: Query again to verify changes if needed
best_practices: ALWAYS include reason parameter for audit trail and compliance
ALWAYS use parameterized queries (%s placeholders) to prevent SQL injection
ALWAYS query current values first with SELECT to preview changes
Use WHERE clause carefully to target specific rows (avoid accidental bulk updates)
Check UNIQUE constraints before inserting (parameter_id + calculator_name for overrides)
Verify FOREIGN KEY references exist before inserting
Set updated_at = NOW() in UPDATE queries for tracking
Use is_active = TRUE/FALSE instead of DELETE for soft deletes
Test query logic with SELECT first, then convert to UPDATE/INSERT
error_handling: Error: Only INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE allowed - Use calculator_database_modify for writes, calculator_database_query for reads
Error: DANGEROUS OPERATION BLOCKED - DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE not allowed via this method for safety
Error: duplicate key value violates unique constraint - Check UNIQUE constraints in schema guide, verify row doesn't already exist
Error: violates foreign key constraint - Verify referenced record exists (parameter_id, option_id, choice_id)
Error: violates check constraint - Review CHECK constraints in schema guide, ensure value meets requirements
Error: cannot cast - Check data types in schema guide, ensure params match column types

tools.description: List all available pre-built queries from QueryLibrary specifically for Calculator Pricing Management category.
